body:
Additionally to this (which should be its own separate issue, however this ticket is useful for getting SPIRV debug info to work on RenderDoc) latest master strips debug info.

Godot must now also be compiled with (see rendering_shader_container_vulkan.h):

```cpp
#define RENDERING_SHADER_CONTAINER_VULKAN_COMPRESSION 0
#define RENDERING_SHADER_CONTAINER_VULKAN_SMOLV 0
```

To get SPIR-V source level debugging working.

> To get SPIR-V source level debugging working.

Should we do this automatically in `DEV_ENABLED` builds, or `DEBUG_ENABLED` builds (or both, so you can enable it for release export templates as well by using `dev_build=yes`)?

Hi @clayjohn I would have to run it, but I don't think this ticket was fixed.

The original problem is that glslang was generating invalid SPIRV which was crashing the RADV driver.

This can be workarounded with:

```cpp
		spvOptions.emitNonSemanticShaderDebugInfo = false;
		spvOptions.emitNonSemanticShaderDebugSource = false
```

Perhaps this got fixed by something else (like a glslang update or shader change).

The thing is that, at some point, this ticket became 2-bugs-in-one because SMOLV was also stripping debug info.

Am experiencing a similar issue on 4.5.1, leading to a segfault:

Command line: `./app.x86_64 --single-window --generate-spirv-debug-info --gpu-validation`

```
Vulkan 1.4.305 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: AMD - AMD Radeon Pro W6600 (RADV NAVI23)
ERROR: Vulkan Debug Report: object - 0
vkCreateShaderModule(): pCreateInfo->pCode (spirv-val produced an error):
OpPhi must appear within a non-entry block before all non-OpPhi instructions (except for OpLine, which can be mixed with OpPhi).
  %263 = OpPhi %bool %252 %206 %262 %254
The Vulkan spec states: If pCode is a pointer to SPIR-V code, pCode must adhere to the validation rules described by the Validation Rules within a Module section of the SPIR-V Environment appendix (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.4.313.0/linux/antora/spec/latest/chapters/shaders.html#VUID-VkShaderModuleCreateInfo-pCode-08737)
   at: _debug_report_callback (drivers/vulkan/rendering_context_driver_vulkan.cpp:665)
ERROR: Vulkan Debug Report: object - 111035763453488
SPIR-V offset 12008: SPIR-V parsing FAILED:
    Unhandled opcode: SpvOpPhi (245)

    12008 bytes into the SPIR-V binary
   at: _debug_report_callback (drivers/vulkan/rendering_context_driver_vulkan.cpp:665)
```

(Note: I tried some fixes including updating glslang on my build of the engine, so this particular trace is not taken from 4.5.1.stable, but the same issue occurs on my hardware on 4.5.1.stable)

Making mesa dump the SPIR-V of the shaders, I can indeed confirm with `spirv-val` that the dumped SPIR-V does not validate.

**EDIT:** Can confirm the above workaround with setting these two options to `false` fixes this for me.

Updating glslang to the version from the latest Vulkan SDK (16.0.0) would fix this, since it's a shader compiler bug that has been fixed upstream since, but updating the other Vulkan SDK components as well sounds like much more work.
Do note the broken (or fixed) shaders are also cached in ~/.local/share/godot/shader_cache, or perhaps project-specific folders though, and that change won't invalidate the cache.
